//build-identity: Notes for the `build` block below. They live OUT here because
electron-builder validates `build` against a strict schema and rejects
any key it does not know, comment or not.
SAPHO is the project (the soft-processor platform); AURORA is its IDE.
Anything that becomes a FILE or a DIRECTORY uses 'SAPHO' alone. An '&' is
legal in Windows paths but breaks unquoted scripts, so 'SAPHO & AURORA'
stays where it is display text (About panel, wordmark).
build.appId MUST match app.setAppUserModelId() in main.js: shortcuts are
stamped with appId, and when the two disagree Windows treats the running
window and the pinned shortcut as different applications, so taskbar
grouping and the jumplist attach to the wrong identity. They diverged
build.productName drives the .exe name, INSTDIR and the shortcuts, so
changing it MOVES the install directory: an already-installed machine
gets the new version ALONGSIDE the old one, not over it.
The npm `name` above is the one never to rename — the updater cache dir
derives from it and holds the delta base. See ARCHITECTURE.md section 11.
//build-fonts: The two `!assets/fonts/*.otf` / `*-LICENSE.txt` lines in build.files are a
guard, not housekeeping. `files` starts at `**/*` and never excluded
assets/, so ANY font left in that directory ships inside the installer.
That already happened once with the Norse wordmark font, whose licence
forbids redistribution: gitignoring it kept it out of the REPO and did
nothing about the DISTRIBUTION (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md records the whole
episode). The wordmark now uses Metamorphous + Noto Sans Runic, both OFL
and both committed as .woff2, so the app needs no .otf at all — anything
with that extension appearing here is a leftover, and these lines keep a
leftover on someone's disk from becoming a licence breach in the .exe.
//overrides: Transitive-only security fixes. None of these is a direct dependency, so
the version we get is whatever an upstream package happens to ask for —
these pins raise the floor to the patched release without waiting for
each upstream to bump its own range.
Prefer this over `npm audit fix`: that command rewrote ~30 packages here,
including a DOWNGRADE of unzipper, which is far more churn than a security
patch should cost on a build that ships to lab machines.
Each entry stays inside the current major so no API changes ride along.
brace-expansion is pinned per-major because three majors coexist in the
tree (minimatch@3 and filelist need the 1.x/2.x API); forcing everything
Remove an entry once every upstream demands the fixed version on its own —
`npm ls <pkg>` shows whether the override is still doing anything.
